summary: The cardholder makes ordinary purchases within the credit limit, receives a monthly statement, and then posts a payment after the due date for less than the required minimum. This scenario probes the late-payment path where the minimum payment obligation is not timely satisfied even though a partial payment eventually arrives.
assumptions: The statement for this cycle closes on 2025-03-31 and sets a payment due date of 2025-04-25.
The new balance on the 2025-03-31 statement is $600.00, so the contractual minimum payment is 3% of the new balance, or $18.00, which is greater than $15.00.
A payment of $10.00 posted on 2025-04-28 is below the required $18.00 minimum and is also late because it posts after the due date.
All card use in this scenario remains within the credit limit, so the credit-limit obligation is treated as performed rather than breached.
Although the late-payment fee is described in the contract, it is not itself one of the user-provided obligation clause ids, so no event in this scenario is bound to that fee clause.
